base.description: UDM-Pro - eight Gigabit LAN, one Gigabit WAN, one 10G SFP+ LAN and one 10G SFP+ WAN port, an empty 3.5 inch NVR drive bay, internal 50 W AC supply, USP-RPS DC input. The data sheet lists one model and no other part number.

description: Ubiquiti UDM-Pro (UniFi Dream Machine Pro) is a fixed 1RU rack gateway. Its front carries a 1.3 inch touchscreen at the left, a door over a 3.5 inch drive bay, eight Gigabit RJ45 LAN ports in two stacked rows, one Gigabit RJ45 WAN port and two 10G SFP+ ports (one WAN, one LAN) in a column, and a recessed factory-reset button. The rear carries the AC power inlet and the USP-RPS DC input for an external redundant supply. The 50 W supply is internal, so it is part of the chassis and not a bay.

gaps.note: The data sheet gives one weight and no ear figure, and no install guide is held. No ear position is stated, none is shipped as default and no kit is listed.
gaps.wanted: The install guide (dl.ui.com/qig/udm-pro) for the ear positions and the one shipped, and the maker's rail kits if any apply.

gaps.note: The page names "(1) 3.5" NVR HDD bay" and the sheet an HDD lamp. No held document says how the door opens, what drive the bay takes, whether one is supplied, or where the lamp sits. The door is panel decor and the lamp is placed on the dot the pictures show on it.
gaps.wanted: The install guide's drive-bay procedure and LED figure.

gaps.note: The sheet's LED table gives each lamp its colours (Ethernet green 1G, amber 10/100M; SFP+ white 10G, green 1G; RPS blue ready) but not whether the two states are steady or blink, and not which jack lamp is which when a jack has more than one.
The legend beside the RPS lamp (USP RPS, OFF, ON) is read off a community drawing at the limit of its resolution, and what the OFF and ON marks are for is not said.
gaps.wanted: The install guide's rear panel and LED table.

gaps.note: The blue mark beside 10 and the small line of text under 11 are not resolved in any picture held, and are not drawn. The blue circle beside 9 is drawn (see provenance wan-mark).
gaps.wanted: A straight-on photograph of the front, or the install guide's port figure.

gaps.note: Neither the data sheet nor the page names a fan or an airflow direction. The NetBox entry says front to rear; both faces carry vent slots; no fan is visible on the rear elevation.
gaps.wanted: The install guide or the maker's thermal description.

gaps.note: No maker photograph of the rear is held: the data sheet shows the front only. The rear is drawn from the community rear elevation.
gaps.wanted: A maker's straight-on photograph of the rear.

gaps.note: No end-of-life notice is in any held document; none was searched for online.

hdd-leds.description: the disk lamp on the drive-bay door

power-input.description: the AC power inlet of the internal supply

rj45.description: the nine built-in Gigabit RJ45 ports as numbered on the faceplate: 1 to 8 LAN, the upper row odd, and 9 WAN (the placements carry role)

rps-input.description: the USP-RPS DC input for an external redundant supply

sfp-plus.description: the two built-in 10G SFP+ ports, 10 (WAN) above and 11 (LAN) below; their ids carry the printed numbers and their position in the group is 1 and 2

sfp-plus-leds.description: the link and activity lamp between the two SFP+ cages, one triangle per cage

name: udm-pro

airflow.note: not stated by the data sheet or the page. The NetBox entry says front to rear; no fan is shown, so no airflow is claimed on the chassis (see the gap).

built-in-power-and-fans.note: Data sheet, Hardware: "Power supply: AC/DC, internal, 50W" and "Power method: (1) Universal AC input, 100-240V AC, 50/60Hz; (1) USP-RPS DC input". The supply is internal, so it is part of the chassis, not a bay and not a component. The sheet says nothing of fans; the slots along the top edges are drawn as vents and no fan is placed (see the gap).

chassis.note: Data sheet, Mechanical: "442.4 x 43.7 x 285.6 mm (17.4 x 1.7 x 11.2")", read as width, height and depth (the 1U height settles it; the switch's sheet prints depth second, this one prints it last: the order differs between the two sheets and each number is read against the model). Weight 3.9 kg (8.6 lb); enclosure "Aluminium CNC, SGCC steel", mount material "SGCC steel". The sheet gives one weight and no with-bracket figure, so it does not say whether ears are in the box; the maker's page says "Rack mount (1U)". The body is modelled at the sheet's 442.4 wide, not 482.6.

colour.note: #c8cacc on both Ubiquiti devices, chosen and not measured: six readings of the plain metal, taken as medians away from ports and text, do not agree. This gateway's community front elevation (ubiquiti-unifi-dream-machine-pro.front.png, the plate left of the drive door, x 100 to 480, y 25 to 85 px) reads #d3d2d5 and its rear elevation (x 300 to 850, y 40 to 95 px) #cbcacd. The USW-Pro-24-PoE's community front elevation reads #e3e5e6 and its rear #c8cacb. The data sheet photograph of this gateway (x 290 to 470, y 722 to 775 of the 1500 px picture) reads #c9c9cb and the switch's #acadaf, its plate being in shade. The two rear elevations and this photograph lie within three levels of #c8cacc; the two front elevations are lighter and the switch's photograph darker. #c8cacc is also the grey of the silver chassis already in the library. Every reading is an estimate of a lit picture, not of the paint.

display.note: Data sheet, Hardware: "LCM display: (1) 1.3" touchscreen", the same part and words as on the USW-Pro-24-PoE, so ubiquiti/lcm-touchscreen-1-3@1. The printed model name under it, "Dream Machine Pro", is drawn as plain text; the brand mark is not.

front-layout.note: estimated - read off the community elevation at the scales under gate-1. LAN block: first column's left edge 309.85, 15.6 mm column step, upper row at 9.5 and lower at 23.3; WAN jack at 388.6, 22.2 (a single jack, latch up, lamp at the upper right); the two SFP+ cages on the registry cell (14.25 wide, 15.0 row pitch) at 405.5, 9.2; touchscreen 23 mm square at 6.5, 10.25; the door 107.2 x 28.1 at 185.9, 7.9; reset pinhole at 426.7, 37.5. The five horizontal slots along the top edge are drawn as plain bars that declare `vent` (see vents). The data sheet photograph agrees on every count.

gate-1.note: The data sheet photograph is oblique (the right side wall is in view), so it is not measured: it supplies counts, arrangement, lamp places and printed legends. The measuring drawing is the community front elevation, 1065 x 106 px: its aspect, 10.05, is 0.7 percent from the body's 442.4 / 43.7 = 10.12, so x is taken at 2.407 px per mm and y at 2.425 from the stated width and height. The RJ45 column pitch then reads 15.6 mm (37.6 px) against the registry cell's 13.97, so the jacks are drawn on the measured pitch and not the registry's; the cell and its cutout are unchanged and the jacks stand 2.9 mm apart. Every position is estimated to about 1 mm.

hdd-bay.note: The page's "(1) 3.5" NVR HDD bay" and the sheet's HDD lamp ("White: disk activity, Amber: disk error") are the sources for a drive bay. The photograph and the drawing show a flat door over it with one dot near its right edge. The door is drawn as panel decor, not a bay: no held document says how a drive is fitted, what the bay accepts, or whether a drive is supplied, so no occupant is modelled. The dot is taken as the HDD lamp; that is a reading of the pictures (see the gap).

jacks.note: Data sheet, LEDs: "Ethernet: Link/ activity, Green: 1G, Amber: 10/100M". Each jack shows one lamp, at the upper right on the upper row and the lower right on the lower row (green in the pictures), so the upper row is turned 180 (latch up) and the lower row takes the lamp-right skin of common/rj45-ganged-link@1. The WAN jack is drawn on the same ganged cell, turned 180, because the library has no single jack with one lamp; its housing in the drawing is 13.6 wide against the cell's 12.7.

legend.note: estimated - "Dream Machine Pro" under the screen is read on both the data sheet strip and the community elevation, which agree on the words and on their length (about 24 mm from the screen's left edge); plain text at 2.7 mm. No brand mark is drawn.

logo.note: The brand mark on the rear label is not drawn: one `logo-zone` region is reserved where the rear elevation shows it. No brand mark is seen on the front elevation, so none is reserved there.

port-numbering.note: Read off the community front elevation at 5x: the upper row of the LAN block prints 1, 3, 5, 7 and the lower row 2, 4, 6, 8; the single jack prints 9 and the SFP+ column 10 above and 11 below, as printed on the metal. The elevation marks 9 and 10 with a small blue dot and gives 11 none; the sheet names a WAN jack and a WAN SFP+, and the NetBox entry labels port 9 WAN 1 and port 10 SFP+ WAN 2, so 9 and 10 are the WAN ports and 1 to 8 and 11 are LAN. Digits are 3 to 4 px high at that size and read with that caution.

ports.note: Data sheet, Hardware: "Networking interface (8) LAN: GbE RJ45 ports (1) WAN: GbE RJ45 port"; "SFP+ interface (1) LAN: 10G SFP+ (1) WAN: 10G SFP+". The page counts nine 1G RJ45 and two 10G SFP+.

rear-layout.note: estimated - read off the community rear elevation (1258 x 128 px, 2.844 px per mm across from the body width and 2.929 down). The USP-RPS socket (two rows of twelve contacts) is 63.5 x 18.0 at 18.4, 19.8 with its USP CONNECT legend under it; the AC inlet plate is 31.1 x 23.4 at 377.8, 12.6 with the C14 in it; three edge screws at 11.6, 220.5 and 429.8, y 37.4; five vent slots along the top. The rating text block at the right and the rating line under the inlet are too small to read and are left out; an empty label outline above the socket is not drawn.

rps.note: Data sheet, LEDs: "RPS: Blue: ready". The lamp is the grey triangle left of the socket in the elevation, with the legend USP RPS, OFF and ON beside it and a small blue dot at ON; which of the two marks is the lamp is not settled (see the gap). The socket is seated as ubiquiti/usp-rps-input@1, which presents the registered key ubiquiti-usp-rps; the plug that enters it is ubiquiti/usp-rps-plug@1, estimated, and no sheet names the cable.

sfp.note: Data sheet, LEDs: "SFP+: Link/ activity, White: 10G, Green: 1G". One white triangle per cage between the two cages, up for the upper and down for the lower, as in the photograph.

sources.note: Ubiquiti data sheet "Datasheet UDM-Pro" (two pages, © 2023 Ubiquiti Inc., PDF created 2023-03-22; https://dl.ui.com/ds/udm-pro.pdf): the Mechanical, Hardware and LEDs tables and its faceplate photograph (923 x 197 px, a three-quarter view). The maker's techspecs.ui.com page data for the model (https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/unifi-cloud-gateways/udm-pro, read 2026-10-26): Form Factor "Rack mount (1U)", dimensions, port layout, "(1) 3.5" NVR HDD bay". The NetBox community devicetype-library entry UniFi-Dream-Machine-Pro.yaml and its front and rear elevation drawings (netbox-community/devicetype-library, read 2026-10-26) are community work, not the maker's; they are used as a second opinion and, for positions, as the only straight-on drawing held. The install guide (dl.ui.com/qig/udm-pro) is not held.

vents.note: estimated - five plain dark bars per face, at the places and sizes read off the community elevations (the data sheet strip shows the same five bars on the front, plain and straight). They are plain rectangles that declare `vent`, not a perforated `pattern: vent` field: a field of 1.0 mm cells in a bar 1.2 or 1.4 mm high drew as a broken chain.

wan-mark.note: estimated - the data sheet strip and the community elevation both show a small blue circle just right of the numeral 9 under the WAN jack, about 2.2 mm across (read at 6x on the elevation: centre 395.0 mm across, 36.6 mm down; the numeral stands at 392.6 there and is kept at 394.95 here, so the circle is set at the same 2.4 mm to its right). It is printed art, not a lamp: the jack's own lamp is the green one at its upper right, carried by the component's led-a as on ports 1 to 8. The same blue circle beside 10 is not drawn (see the gap).
